subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs (OpenAI/Anthropic) - FintechCo
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Lara Gomez <lara.gomez@fintechco.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@fintechco.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-02-14T16:32:00-08:00
Subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs (OpenAI/Anthropic) - FintechCo

Hi Lara / Samir —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we're aligned: 

Pain points you shared:
- Cost volatility and token spend on current OpenAI usage (some endpoints cost >3x during peak volumes).
- Latency spikes for synchronous customer workflows during batch settlement windows.
- Data governance concerns: wanting customer data to never leave the VPC and stricter KMS controls for keys.

Current stack / usage notes you mentioned:
- Primary inference today: OpenAI for chat completion and Anthropic for assistant-style tasks (safety layer).
- ~1M requests/month; 95th percentile latency target for API calls is 600ms.
- Heavy use of streaming responses, function-calling integration, and structured JSON outputs for downstream parsers.

Success criteria for a migration: 
- Parity of function-calling and streaming behavior or a compatible pattern for caller-side integration.
- Total cost of inference <= current spend (or clear plan to reach parity within 3 months).
- Deployment into a Private/VPC environment with KMS/HSM integration and audit logs.
- No regression on safety checks currently handled by Anthropic (either via model choice or a Redwood-hosted policy).

Compatibility checklist we discussed (shortlist ideas):
- Model API compatibility: adapter for OpenAI-style completions + function call semantics.
- Model shortlist for early evaluation: Llama 3 family (higher-quality variants), Mistral-instruct, and Claude-like open reimplementations where available.
- Quantization/throughput considerations: 8-bit/4-bit quantization needs testing for latency targets.

Next steps / proposed plan:
1) Redwood to send a migration playbook and a short checklist of dev changes (function-calling mappings, streaming client hints). I’ve attached the playbook and a sample MSA redline template.
2) Technical deep-dive with your engineering team next week (30–45m) — we suggest Mar 2 or Mar 3; Aditya will lead the session to cover runtime compatibility and perf expectations.
3) Pilot: small subset of traffic (2–5%) routed to a dedicated Redwood Private deployment for 2–4 weeks to validate latency and safety regressions.
4) Pricing: we’ll provide a draft pricing scenario for Dedicated/Private (reserved + burst) and a cost comparison vs current OpenAI spend.

Please reply with any corrections. If that looks right, can you confirm availability for the technical deep-dive and share the email for the engineers you want looped in?

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0187
Redwood Inference

Marissa —

Thanks for the thorough recap. This looks good and captures the discussion. A couple clarifications: 
- The 600ms SLO is for user-facing chat flows; internal batch processes can tolerate up to 2s.
- Our security team requires that any Private deployment supports customer-managed keys (AWS KMS) and full audit log export (S3).
- We absolutely need function-calling parity for our payments reconciliation flow — that’s non-negotiable for the first pilot.

We’re available for a technical deep-dive on Mar 3, 10:00–10:45 PT. Please invite Aditya and Rishi from your side, and I’ll loop in our lead infra engineer (samir.patel@fintechco.com) and security (sec-lead@fintechco.com).

One ask: can you include a short compatibility matrix in the playbook that maps OpenAI function-calling -> Redwood adapter expectations? That will help our devs review pre-call.

Thanks,
Lara
Director of Product, FintechCo

Hi all —

Thanks for the invite. A few quick technical notes ahead of tomorrow’s deep-dive: 

1) Function-calling: Redwood’s adapter supports OpenAI-style function schema today. There are two integration patterns we typically recommend:
   - Direct adapter mode: minimal change to callers; Redwood translates function calls to model prompts and returns structured JSON.
   - Client-side shim: small helper lib (JS/Python) that mimics OpenAI client and maps to Redwood endpoints; slightly more control for retry/backpressure.

2) Streaming: We preserve chunked streaming semantics; for some quantized backends we buffer small segments to maintain latency SLOs — we’ll show a demo.

3) Safety: We can chain a safety model (Anthropic-style classifier) as a policy layer, or run rule-based checks pre-send. For the pilot, we recommend Redwood-hosted safety policy + your current Anthropic safety pass to compare outputs side-by-side.

4) Models to evaluate (shortlist):
   - Llama 3 13B instruct (high quality, likely parity for many prompts)
   - Mistral-Instruct v1 (strong instruction-following)
   - RedLlama-variant (internal-tested customization for finance prompts)

I attached a short tech checklist and the items I’d like Samir to paste into the invite: example function-calling payload, streaming client sample, expected 95th latency target.

See you on Mar 3.

Rishi
Lead Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
